results.name: Chair Pose
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and raise both arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your arms extended overhead.
Hold the position while keeping your heels on the floor, and your weight evenly distributed across both feet.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Sit your hips back as if lowering onto a chair.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes without allowing them to collapse inward.
Engage your core to improve balance and stability.
Inhale as you lower into the pose and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Chair Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

results.name: Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with your hips resting on your heels, face forward with your hands to your sides.
Lower your torso toward the floor and slowly extend both hands to one side while keeping your hips resting on your heels, resting your forehead on your hands.
Hold the stretch when you feel it along the side of your upper back and torso.
Return your to your starting position, repeat the stretch to the opposite side, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips resting on your heels throughout the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them toward your ears
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull along your side.
Inhale in the center and exhale as you reach to each side.
results.description: Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Lower Back.

results.name: Child Pose Arms on Side
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with your knees slightly apart and your hands resting by your sides.
Sit your hips back onto your heels as you lower your chest toward your thighs, allowing your forehead to rest on the floor.
Extend your arms alongside your body with your palms facing upward and relax your shoulders.
Hold the stretch, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your hips resting on your heels throughout the stretch.
Allow your shoulders to relax completely as your arms rest beside your body.
Avoid lifting your hips away from your heels.
Inhale deeply and exhale as you settle further into the stretch.
results.description: Child Pose Arms on Side is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes.

results.name: Child Pose Elbows on Block
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with two yoga blocks placed in front of you. Rest both elbows on each block and bring your hands together behind your head.
Sit your hips back toward your heels as you lower your chest toward the floor.
Allow your elbows to remain on the block while gently sinking your chest to deepen the stretch through your shoulders and upper back.
Hold the stretch, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your elbows supported on the block throughout the stretch.
Keep your hips moving toward your heels as you lower your chest.
Avoid rounding your lower back excessively.
Inhale before lowering and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
results.description: Child Pose Elbows on Block is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Crescent Moon Pose
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and your back knee resting on the floor. Bend your back knee and reach behind you to grasp your back foot with both hands.
Gently draw your back heel toward your glutes while keeping your chest lifted and your hips facing forward.
Hold the stretch until you feel a comfortable stretch along the front of your back thigh and hip.
Release your foot with control, return to the starting position, and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your front knee directly above your ankle.
Engage your core to help maintain balance and alignment.
Keep your chest lifted and avoid leaning excessively forward.
Inhale before deepening the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your foot closer.
results.description: Crescent Moon Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

results.name: Criss Cross Bow Tie Pose
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended. Cross one arm over the other, palms facing down.
Walk your hands out in opposite directions as far as possible, dipping your head and chest toward the floor.
Relax your shoulders and hold the position until you feel a comfortable stretch across the back of your shoulder and upper back.
Release the stretch slowly and repeat with the opposite arm crossed underneath.
tips: Stretch only until you feel a gentle pull across the shoulder and upper back.
Keep both shoulders relaxed throughout the stretch.
Avoid lifting your torso or twisting your hips.
Inhale slowly and exhale as you relax into the position.
results.description: Criss Cross Bow Tie Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Rotator Cuff.

results.name: Crow Pose
instructions: Begin in a deep squat with your feet slightly wider than hip width apart. Place both hands flat on the floor shoulder width apart in front of you.
Lean your body forward and position the insides of your knees against the outsides of your elbows.
Shift your weight onto your hands and lift both feet off the floor, balancing with your knees supported slightly above your elbows.
Hold the position briefly, then slowly lower your feet back to the floor and return to the starting position.
tips: Spread your fingers wide to create a stable base of support.
Keep your gaze slightly forward rather than directly at the floor to help maintain balance.
Shift your weight forward gradually until your feet lift naturally.
Inhale before shifting your weight forward and exhale as you lift your feet from the floor.
results.description: Crow Pose is an advanced multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Double Pigeon Pose
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Bend your right knee and position your shin horizontally in front of you. Lift the other leg and stack your top shin over the bottom shin so both shins are nearly parallel.
Sit upright with a long spine and gently rest your forearms on your top shin while relaxing your hips. Lean into your forearms applying slight pressure on the top leg.
Hold the stretch, then uncross your legs with control and repeat with the opposite leg on top.
tips: Relax your hips and allow your knees to lower naturally without forcing them.
If one hip lifts off the floor, reduce the depth of the position until both hips are evenly supported.
Stack your shins as evenly as your flexibility allows.
Inhale as you lengthen your spine and exhale as you relax deeper into the stretch.
results.description: Double Pigeon Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Downward Dog Toe to Heel
instructions: Stand upright with your feet at shoulder width apart and raise both arms overhead. Bend forward, place your hands on the floor, in front of your feet with a slight bend in your knees.
Walk your feet backward until your body forms an inverted V shape. Keep your hands and feet at shoulder width apart, and lift your hips upward.
Press your left heel into the floor as you bend the right knee, placing your foot in a position where the toes of your right foot align with heel of your left leg.
Hold for a few seconds, then walk your feet back to the starting position. Stand up and alternate sides.
tips: Press firmly through your palms and spread your fingers for stability.
Keep your neck relaxed and your gaze directed toward your feet or between your legs.
Lift your hips upward to lengthen your spine throughout the movement.
Inhale as you prepare and exhale each time you press a heel toward the floor.
results.description: Downward Dog Toe to Heel is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Upper Back.

results.name: Downward Dog With Fingers Facing Feet
instructions: Stand upright with your feet at shoulder width apart and raise both arms overhead. Bend forward, place your hands on the floor, with your fingers pointing at your feet and a slight bend in your knees.
Walk your feet backward until your body forms an inverted V shape. Keep your hands and feet planted on the floor, lifting your hips upward.
Straighten your arms and legs, keeping a slight bend in each joint as you lift your hips toward the ceiling and gently press your chest toward your thighs.
Hold the stretch, then walk your feet back toward your hands and slowly return to a standing position.
tips: Spread your fingers and press evenly through your palms to support your wrists.
Reduce the amount of hand rotation if you feel discomfort in your wrists.
Keep your head relaxed between your arms.
Inhale as you move into the stretch and exhale as you deepen it.
results.description: Downward Dog With Fingers Facing Feet is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back, Hamstrings.
